notes: §1985:IX.3.2.4 GR3: "The DATA RECORDS clause of the Indexed I-O module is the same as the DATA RECORDS clause for the Sequential I-O module", whose specifications are that it "serves only as documentation for the names of data records" (§1985:VII.3.5.1), that data-name-1 "must have an 01 level-number record description" (§1985:VII.3.5.3 SR1) and that "all data records within a file share the same area" (§1985:VII.3.5.4 GR2). The one grammar rule dataRecordsClause is admitted in the indexed format by its Rows row, BindFileSection calls ScreenDataRecords (since kb/Work PB5070 landed) to refuse a name that is not an 01 of THIS entry (COBOL6849), and VisitDataRecordsClause refuses the clause from 2002 (COBOL0873); the clause has no run-time effect, the sharing of the area being the record model's. Probed at --std 85 over an indexed file, 2026-11-14 tree dc1f2dcce8: (b) DATA RECORD IS R, DATA RECORDS ARE R R2, R2 R, R R and DATA RECORD R2 run; refused with COBOL6849: an 05 item, an ODO table element, another FD's 01, a Working-Storage 01, an undefined name, the file-name; R OF F (a data-name of a format may not be qualified, §1985:IV glossary 'Data-Name') COBOL1970, a literal and ZERO COBOL5506, a subscript COBOL0001; with two FDs each holding 01 R, DATA RECORD IS R in each compiles and runs (the unqualifiable name is the entry's own record); (c) the clause is refused at 2002 and 2023; (a)(d) the ODO record and an 11-character elementary 01 share one area: after reading the ODO record (N=3) R2 shows the same characters; (e) a sequential file with the clause writes and reads, and on the indexed file a READ of a missing key gives INVALID KEY with status 23, the next OPEN of a missing file (no FILE STATUS) terminates with status 35. The prior PARTIAL (SR1 never asked) is fixed by PB5070. The witness reads back an indexed record under DATA RECORD IS naming its 01 and displays K001 ABCD. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5070 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5070 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-03.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-03-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "The DATA RECORDS clause is an obsolete element in Standard COBOL because it is to be deleted from the next revision"; 2023: "No DATA RECORDS clause among the 13.4.5 file description entry rules or the 13.18 clauses; the clause was deleted". The DATA RECORDS clause was obsolete in 1985 and slated for deletion. No 2023 file description or clause candidate mentions it, so the feature is gone.
